title: Narrative over Numbers: The Identifiable Victim Effect and its Amplification Under Alignment and Reasoning in Large Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing hypothetical charitable donation allocations and affective self-reports generated by LLMs in response to prompts describing specific, narratively detailed victims versus aggregate, statistically described groups of victims.

Manipulating the cultural and geographic distance of the victim (e.g., Near/US, Middle/Eastern Europe, Far/Sub-Saharan Africa) in the prompt while holding victim severity and narrative detail constant to measure in-group versus out-group resource allocation disparities.
